title: International Court of Justice rules Myanmar committed genocide against Rohingya
seoTitle: ICJ rules Myanmar committed Rohingya genocide
dek: The International Court of Justice has ruled that Myanmar committed genocide against its Rohingya Muslim minority during a 2017 military campaign.
happened: On 19 November 2026, the International Court of Justice delivered a historic judgment stating that Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya minority in northern Rakhine state. According to court president Yuji Iwasawa, the 15-judge panel decided by a 9-6 majority that security forces killed thousands of civilians, carried out widespread sexual violence, committed extreme violence against children, and targeted fleeing people. The court noted that evidence showed roughly 10,000 Rohingya were killed during the 2017 operations, which the military initially launched as a clearance campaign following an insurgent attack. The case was originally brought to the UN court by Gambia in 2019 under the 1948 Genocide Convention. This marks the first time the UN court has held a state responsible for genocide. Following the decision, reactions varied globally: the UK announced it was expelling Myanmar's defence attache and calling for a UN Security Council session, while the US stated it was examining the judgment and cautioned against politicising the court.

sides.says: The 15-judge panel ruled by a 9-6 majority that Myanmar "has committed genocide against the Rohingya group in northern Rakhine state, in violation of its obligations under the Genocide Convention." The court concluded that security forces acted with the intent to destroy a substantial part of the Rohingya population.

Gambia initiated the legal proceedings at the International Court of Justice in 2019, asking the court to rule that Myanmar breached the 1948 Genocide Convention, halt illegal activities against the Rohingya, and punish those responsible.
British Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband announced that the UK was expelling Myanmar's defence attache and "calling urgently for a UN Security Council session to discuss the judgment."
The EU stated that Myanmar must fully implement the ruling "without delay" and that "compliance with ICJ's decisions is not optional, it is an obligation under international law."

next: The International Court of Justice ruling is final and cannot be appealed. Discussions are anticipated at the UN Security Council following requests from member states.
summary: The International Court of Justice has ruled that Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya minority during military operations in 2017. Decided by a 9-6 vote in a case brought by Gambia, the historic judgment marks the first time the UN’s highest court has held a sovereign state responsible for genocide. The court found that security forces killed thousands of civilians and carried out widespread sexual and extreme violence with the intent to destroy the Rohingya population. Governments around the world have responded with varied diplomatic measures and calls for accountability.
